title: 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Atrial Fibrillation (JACC 2024 publication)
fundamental_guidance_point: For atrial fibrillation patients who are candidates for anticoagulation and have neither moderate-to-severe rheumatic mitral stenosis nor a mechanical heart valve, the 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS guideline recommends a direct oral anticoagulant rather than warfarin (Class 1, Level A).
guidance_quote_location: Section 6.3.1, Antithrombotic Therapy, recommendation 2 (COR 1, LOE A); supporting references 1-7; section-specific bibliography reference 3 is Granger et al. (ARISTOTLE).
x1_study_title: Granger et al., Apixaban versus warfarin in patients with atrial fibrillation (NEJM 2011)
picot_population: 18,201 patients with atrial fibrillation and at least one additional risk factor for stroke; patients with moderate/severe mitral stenosis or mechanical prosthetic valves were not the indicated population.
picot_intervention: Apixaban 5 mg twice daily (dose-reduction rules applied to eligible patients in trial).
picot_outcomes: Stroke or systemic embolism: 1.27%/year with apixaban vs 1.60%/year with warfarin, HR 0.79 (95% CI 0.66-0.95); major bleeding: 2.13%/year vs 3.09%/year, HR 0.69 (0.60-0.80); all-cause death HR 0.89 (0.80-0.99).
picot_time: Median follow-up 1.8 years; randomized, double-blind noninferiority trial with superiority testing.
x1_effect_size: Stroke or systemic embolism: 1.27%/year with apixaban vs 1.60%/year with warfarin, HR 0.79 (95% CI 0.66-0.95); major bleeding: 2.13%/year vs 3.09%/year, HR 0.69 (0.60-0.80); all-cause death HR 0.89 (0.80-0.99).
x1_uncertainty: Stroke/systemic embolism HR 0.79 (95% CI 0.66-0.95); major bleeding HR 0.69 (0.60-0.80).
x1_limitations: Supports apixaban specifically, not every available DOAC; trial eligibility, renal function, drug interactions, adherence, hemorrhage risk and patient-specific contraindications require independent clinical evaluation. Industry funded.
notes: ONE selected reference document and one directly supporting X1 (bounded applicability). Entire curriculum/reference-document inventory NOT exhaustive; human review and cross-track mapping pending.

subtopic: Chronic kidney disease: SGLT2 inhibitors for risk reduction
title: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of CKD
fundamental_guidance_point: KDIGO 2024 recommends SGLT2 inhibition for adults with CKD when eGFR is at least 20 mL/min/1.73 m2 and urine ACR is at least 200 mg/g (recommendation 3.7.2, grade 1A). The guideline also offers a separate heart-failure indication, which is outside the selected X1 comparison.
guidance_quote_location: KDIGO 2024 CKD guideline, Section 3.7, Recommendation 3.7.2, Kidney International 105(Suppl 4S), p. S159; DAPA-CKD discussed in supporting narrative; Heerspink et al. cited in guideline bibliography.
x1_study_title: Heerspink et al., Dapagliflozin in Patients with Chronic Kidney Disease (NEJM 2020)
picot_population: 4,304 adults with CKD (with or without type 2 diabetes), eGFR 25-75 mL/min/1.73 m2 and urine ACR 200-5000 mg/g.
picot_intervention: Dapagliflozin 10 mg once daily added to standard CKD treatment.
picot_comparator: Matching placebo added to standard CKD treatment.
picot_outcomes: Composite of sustained >=50% eGFR fall, kidney failure, or renal/cardiovascular death: 197/2152 (9.2%) vs 312/2152 (14.5%); HR 0.61 (95% CI 0.51-0.72), NNT 19 (95% CI 15-27) over follow-up.
picot_time: Median follow-up 2.4 years; randomized double-blind trial stopped early for efficacy.
x1_effect_size: Composite of sustained >=50% eGFR fall, kidney failure, or renal/cardiovascular death: 197/2152 (9.2%) vs 312/2152 (14.5%); HR 0.61 (95% CI 0.51-0.72), NNT 19 (95% CI 15-27) over follow-up.
x1_uncertainty: Composite kidney/CV outcome HR 0.61 (95% CI 0.51-0.72); NNT 19 (95% CI 15-27).
x1_limitations: No direct randomization evidence for eGFR 20-24 or nonalbuminuric CKD in this specific trial; stopping early may affect estimated benefit and event precision. Guideline generalizes from several RCTs and meta-analyses, not DAPA-CKD alone.
notes: ONE selected reference document and one directly supporting X1 (bounded applicability). Entire curriculum/reference-document inventory NOT exhaustive; human review and cross-track mapping pending.
